decisions.reason: The Hero V supplies the reference reach, but the source changes only how that reach is preserved in the lowercase second V; the Hero V geometry remains unchanged.
The subtle lowercase-v reach refinement does not change the existing shared-terminal rule, and the separate É-overlay clause does not alter its already established literal shared-signature semantics.
The source's É-accent refinement is already fully represented by the same-message MODIFY requiring an exact one-to-one overlay match; the lowercase-v reach change adds nothing to this Requirement.
The source refines the lowercase second V and É accent, not the deferred architectural construction of the E and L letterforms.
A subtle, almost imperceptible extension of the lowercase v's right arm does not change its established smaller and subordinate prominence relative to the Hero V.
The geometric reach refinement does not change the deferred champagne material treatment or its role.
The source does not change spacing or the requirement that the full wordmark read as one unified mark.
The requested É construction diagram is specific evidence for accent derivation and does not modify the general obligation to provide brief design rationale with review rounds.
